narration: Welcome to the Arms & Armour gallery. This is the Battle Axe of Nadir Shah, an Indo‑Persian weapon from 1739 CE, crafted from metal and richly adorned with gold and silver. The axe head bears Quranic verses and the inscription “Sahib‑e‑Qiran Nadir,” while the octagonal handle is embellished with intricate floral work in gold and silver. It is a tangible reminder of Nadir Shah’s 1739 campaign that sacked Delhi, taking treasures such as the Peacock Throne and the Koh‑i‑Noor diamond. The National Museum acquired it as accession number 58.47/3, and it remains in the care of the Government of India, Ministry of Culture.
